### Observed differences

- In the later window, A10 is executed far more often and much later in the case: it appears in about 60 in 100 cases (119 of 200) versus about 20 in 100 (41 of 200) before, its mean occurrences per trace rose from about 0.21 to 0.64, and its median relative position moved from about 0.38 to about 0.97 of the case's events. [OCC003, POS001]
- In the later window, A10 typically forms a segment near the end between A45 and A46: about 91 in 100 of A10's observed outgoing transitions now go to A46 (about 20 in 100 before), A45 sends about 57 in 100 of its outgoing transitions to A10 (about 4 in 100 before), and the pairs A45→A10 and A10→A46 are one step apart in about 98–99 in 100 of observed instances; A25, A26, A27, A28 and A40 now precede A10 in about 53–55 in 100 cases each, versus about 5–12 in 100 before. [DIR004, DIR013, LAG001, LAG015, REL003, REL009]
- In the later window, A19 and A20 occur earlier (mean relative position about 0.36 versus about 0.51–0.52) and are rerouted: about 93–95 in 100 of their observed outgoing transitions now go to A25, whereas before roughly half went to A27 and half to A28; they now precede A25, A26 and A27 in about half of all cases (e.g., A19 before A25 in about 52 in 100 cases, from none before), where previously they followed these activities in about 43–57 in 100 cases. [POS002, POS003, DIR006, DIR007, REL010, REL013]
- In the later window, A40 no longer feeds A25 directly: its outgoing transitions split about 48 and 45 in 100 between A19 and A20 (about 84 in 100 went to A25 before), and A40 is now adjacent to them, one step apart in about 94 in 100 of instances versus five steps before. [DIR011, LAG011, LAG012]
- The sequence behind A25 tightened once A19/A20 left it: A26 is now followed by A27 in about 97 in 100 of its outgoing transitions (about 53 in 100 before, with A19/A20 taking most of the rest), A27 is followed by A28 in about 98 in 100 (about 45 in 100 before), and A26 reaches A28 in two rather than three steps in about 96 in 100 of instances. [DIR008, DIR009, LAG008, LAG009, LAG010]
- In the later window, A04 and A06 are executed in fewer cases: A04 in about 10 in 100 cases (21 of 200) versus about 21 in 100 (41 of 200), and A06 in about 6 in 100 (12 of 200) versus about 19 in 100 (38 of 200); their outgoing profiles are reshuffled, but the later profiles rest on only 22 and 12 observed outgoing transitions. [OCC001, OCC002, DIR002, DIR003]
- A02's transition to A44, about 31 in 100 of its observed outgoing transitions before, was not observed in the later window, where its outgoing transitions spread across many activities on a base of 20 observed transitions. [DIR001]

### Inference

Support level: Supported hypothesis

The evidence supports the possibility that routing around several activities was restructured in the later window: A19 and A20, which previously ran after A25/A26 and led mainly into A27/A28, now run before A25 — typically entered from A40, which previously went to A25 directly — with A26 → A27 → A28 following in tight succession; A10, previously a mid-process activity in about 20 in 100 cases, now appears in about 60 in 100 cases as the late segment A45 → A10 → A46; and A04 and A06 are executed in fewer cases (roughly half and a third of their earlier participation). [OCC001, OCC002, OCC003, DIR006, DIR007, DIR011, REL010, REL013, LAG011, POS001, DIR004, DIR013, LAG001]

The placement claims rest on relational and positional evidence rather than frequency alone: the order reversals are direct (A19/A20 before A25/A26/A27 rose from zero to about half of cases while the reverse order collapsed to near zero), the new adjacencies are direct (A40→A19/A20, A45→A10 and A10→A46 one step apart in about 94–99 in 100 of instances), and the routing, participation and position indicators agree on the same activities. The 53 qualifying items far exceed the fewer than 1 expected by chance among the 144 tested units, and each difference exceeds about 99.5 in 100 random re-splits, so the pattern as a whole is unlikely if nothing had changed. [REL010, REL013, LAG011, LAG001, DIR008, OCC003, POS001]

Limitations: the windows are 200-trace samples, so part of the frequency shifts — particularly the declines of A04 and A06 and their reshuffled outgoing profiles, which rest on 22 and 12 later-window transitions — could reflect sampling differences in variant frequencies rather than a structural change; a few lag items rest on a single observation on one side (LAG003, LAG006, LAG007); items describing the same behaviour (for instance REL003–REL008, which all capture A10's new late position) are not independent confirmations; and routing shares cover only observed outgoing transitions, so an unobserved transition such as A02→A44 is not proven absent. [OCC001, OCC002, DIR002, DIR003, LAG003, LAG006, LAG007, REL003, DIR001]
